Android from the foundation · Puzzle 18 of 19

The ViewModel outlives the screen

In puzzle 17, turning the phone threw away the Activity and everything in its fields. Here's the object made to survive that, and where it waits while the new Activity is built.

The problem

In puzzle 17, a configuration change replaced your Activity with a new one, and the counter in its fields went back to 0. Now imagine the field held a list that took two seconds to download. Every time the user turns the phone, it's gone, and you download it again. The process survived: is there somewhere in it that outlives one Activity object?

See it

Save this diagram as a GIF

The building block

A ViewModel is an object made to hold one screen's data. You write it as a class built on ViewModel, and it can do the slow work itself, like the download:

class ListViewModel : ViewModel() {
    val items = download()   // runs once, when the ViewModel is created
}

// in the Activity:
val vm: ListViewModel by viewModels()

The word by in that last line hands the job of finding the ViewModel to viewModels(), which doesn't create a new one each time. Each Activity keeps its ViewModels in a ViewModelStore: a small map from a name to a ViewModel. viewModels() looks in the store first and creates the ViewModel only if it isn't there yet.

The trick is what happens to the store. When the Activity is destroyed only to be recreated, ActivityThreadWhen an Activity is destroyed only to be recreated, ActivityThread keeps what it hands over (including the ViewModelStore), then gives it to the new Activity in attach(). 6119 if (getNonConfigInstance) { 6120 r.lastNonConfigurationInstances = r.activity.retainNonConfigurationInstances(); … 4180 activity.attach(…, r.lastNonConfigurationInstances, config, …);ActivityThread.java, lines 6120 and 4180 · AOSP frameworks/base ↗, Android's own code in your process that creates and destroys your Activities, keeps the store and hands it to the new Activity. Same store, same ViewModel, same count. Nothing crosses Binder: it all stays in your process's memory.

When the Activity is destroyed for good, for example the user pressed the Back button to leave the screen, no new Activity is coming. Then the store is cleared, and each ViewModel's onCleared() runs: your chance to stop work it started, like an unfinished download. The code that ships with ViewModel decides between the two with one check: at destroy, clear the store only if isChangingConfigurations is false (it's true when this destroy is only to recreate the Activity).

So a ViewModel lives as long as the user keeps that screen: the screen they see stays the same, while the Activity objects behind it are replaced. But it still lives in your process. If the process itself is gone, so is the ViewModel. What survives that is the next part of this module (coming soon).

The analogy

Before the room is torn down to be rebuilt, the clerk carries its locker out and sets it in the new room. If the room is closed for good, the locker is emptied instead.

Check yourself

A ViewModel downloads a list when it's created, like the one above. The user turns the phone twice. How many times is the list downloaded?

Not quite. The Activities are new, but the ViewModel waits in the store and is handed over.

Right. The store survives configuration changes, so the ViewModel and its list do too.

Not quite. The store is cleared only when the screen closes for good, not on a configuration change.

Why is the store cleared when the user presses Back, but not when they turn the phone?

Not quite. Speed has nothing to do with it: the code checks whether the Activity is being destroyed only to be recreated. Re-read that part ↑

Not quite. The process can live on. Only that screen is finished.

Right. Clear the store unless a new Activity will take it.

What's the difference between a ViewModel and the ViewModelStore?

Not quite. No: it stays in your own process, handed from the old Activity to the new one.

Not quite. The store is a container; the ViewModels are what's inside it.

Right. One map, many ViewModels, all in your process.

Sources

  • AndroidX source: ComponentActivity (on ON_DESTROY: if (!isChangingConfigurations) { viewModelStore.clear() }; the new Activity takes the store from lastNonConfigurationInstance)
  • AndroidX source: ViewModelStore (a mutableMapOf<Any?, ViewModel>())
  • AOSP: ActivityThread.java (r.lastNonConfigurationInstances = r.activity.retainNonConfigurationInstances(), then passed to activity.attach(…))
  • Android Developers: ViewModel overview

What you now know

A ViewModel lives in its Activity's ViewModelStore. On a configuration change, ActivityThread keeps the store and hands it to the new Activity, all inside your process. When the screen closes for good, the store is cleared and onCleared() runs.
